To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We give a string theory construction of spherical domain walls in 4d M. space connecting different amounts of 4d supersymmetry, and we show that these walls have tension lower than the 10d Planck scale.

we found examples of string compactification that can be connected to each other by spherical domain walls whose tension is lower than the 3d or 4d Plancks scale, and that the stringy description of these walls can be given in terms of configurations of wrapped Dirchlet and NS brane.
we constructed supersymmetry changing domain walls in string theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of domain wall solutions to 4d supergravities.
the construction and study of supersymmetric string compactifications with various amounts of supersymmetries.
the study of the dynamics of the scalar fields of a string theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the string theory landscape is not only vast but also very complex.
there are no stable, supersymmetric, nonsingular domain wall solutions in string theory, and that the only stable solutions are the trivial ones.
the 4d = N supersymmetric vacua are connected by 5d = N - 1 supersymmetric domain walls, and the tension of these walls is tunably low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have constructed the first examples of 4d M-theory compactifications to Minkowski space that are supersymmetric and can be connected by a spherical domain wall with tension lower than the 10d Planck scale.
we show that the stringy picture for the domain walls is consistent with a 4d field theory interpretation in terms of the world-volume theory of the wrapped branes.
the string theory description of the supersymmetry changing domain walls is a generalization of the D3-brane domain walls in type IIB string theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supersymmetry is not an intrinsic property of a 4d vacuum but rather a property of a domain wall connecting different vacua.
supersymmetry can be broken by the dynamics of the vacuum, rather than by a symmetry breaking Higgs sector.
supersymmetry changing domain walls can be much lighter than the string scale, and that their tension is determined by the difference in energy between the vacua they connect.
